# Story 10 — SLA, Automation & Notifications (Story: 10)

---

- Stories 01–09 completed and merged into `main`. This story directly extends:
  - Story 07's `Ticket` domain / `TicketsController` CRUD.
  - Story 08's manual assignment path and `GET /api/tickets/assignable-users` endpoint.
  - Story 09's `TicketNote` entity and `POST /api/tickets/{id}/notes` endpoint, plus `TicketDetailPage.tsx` / `TicketsPage.tsx`.
  - Story 05's `AuditLogger` conventions.

## Story Goal

Add SLA tracking, automatic ticket assignment, ticket-level escalation, and in-app notifications to the CRM using **only lazy (read-time) computation** on the server plus a **client-side polling bell** — no background jobs, no real-time infra, no new packages.

Concretely:

1. Persist two new nullable timestamps on `Ticket` (`FirstRespondedAtUtc`, `ResolvedAtUtc`) and add a new `Notification` table.
2. Compute `responseDueAtUtc` / `resolutionDueAtUtc` / `isEscalated` on-the-fly in `GET /api/tickets` and `GET /api/tickets/{id}`.
3. Auto-assign new tickets to the least-loaded Agent/Admin when the caller omits `assignedToUserId`.
4. Create `Notification` rows when a ticket is assigned to a user or when a ticket newly becomes escalated (with per-ticket de-duplication for escalation).
5. Add a header notification bell in the App Shell that polls unread count and lists recent notifications.
6. Surface SLA due-dates and an escalation badge in the tickets list and detail views, EN + AR.

**Explicitly out of scope:** admin-editable SLA targets, real-time push, background schedulers, manual "escalate" action, notification preferences/settings, any Story 11–14 content.

## Product rules (from story)

**Fixed SLA targets (this story — not configurable):**

| Priority | Response | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Urgent | 1 h | 4 h |
| High   | 2 h | 8 h |
| Normal | 4 h | 24 h |
| Low    | 8 h | 48 h |

- `ResponseDueAtUtc = CreatedAtUtc + responseTarget(Priority)` — **computed**, never persisted.
- `ResolutionDueAtUtc = CreatedAtUtc + resolutionTarget(Priority)` — **computed**, never persisted.
- `FirstRespondedAtUtc` — set exactly once, when the **first `TicketNote`** is created on the ticket. Field edits via `PUT /api/tickets/{id}` do not count.
- `ResolvedAtUtc` — set to `now` on `Status` transition **into** `"Closed"`; cleared to `null` on transition **away from** `"Closed"`.
- `IsEscalated` — computed, never persisted. `true` iff `Status != "Closed"` AND ((`now > ResponseDueAtUtc` AND `FirstRespondedAtUtc is null`) OR (`now > ResolutionDueAtUtc` AND `ResolvedAtUtc is null`)).
- `Status` remains exactly `"Open" | "InProgress" | "Closed"` — do **not** add an `"Escalated"` status.
- Auto-assign only when the request omits `assignedToUserId`. An explicit `null` in the request body is treated as "leave unassigned" and preserves current Story 08 behavior.

### 3 — SLA target lookup constant

**File:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/TicketsController.cs`

Add (near line 17, mirroring `AllowedStatuses` style):

```csharp
private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, (TimeSpan Response, TimeSpan Resolution)> SlaTargets =
    new Dictionary<string, (TimeSpan, TimeSpan)>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
    {
        ["Urgent"] = (TimeSpan.FromHours(1),  TimeSpan.FromHours(4)),
        ["High"]   = (TimeSpan.FromHours(2),  TimeSpan.FromHours(8)),
        ["Normal"] = (TimeSpan.FromHours(4),  TimeSpan.FromHours(24)),
        ["Low"]    = (TimeSpan.FromHours(8),  TimeSpan.FromHours(48)),
    };

private static (DateTime response, DateTime resolution) ComputeDueDates(DateTime createdUtc, string priority)
{
    var t = SlaTargets.TryGetValue(priority, out var v) ? v : SlaTargets["Normal"];
    return (createdUtc + t.Response, createdUtc + t.Resolution);
}

private static bool ComputeIsEscalated(
    string status, DateTime responseDueUtc, DateTime resolutionDueUtc,
    DateTime? firstRespondedAtUtc, DateTime? resolvedAtUtc, DateTime nowUtc)
{
    if (status == "Closed") return false;
    if (firstRespondedAtUtc is null && nowUtc > responseDueUtc) return true;
    if (resolvedAtUtc is null && nowUtc > resolutionDueUtc) return true;
    return false;
}
```

### 7 — `POST /api/tickets` (Create): auto-assignment + assigned notification

**File:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/TicketsController.cs`, `Create` handler (~lines 310–360)

- **Only** when `request.AssignedToUserId is null` (the property was omitted or null in the incoming request), call a new helper:

```csharp
private static async Task<User?> PickLeastLoadedAssigneeAsync(AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct)
{
    var candidates = await db.Users
        .Where(u => u.UserRoles.Any(ur => ur.Role!.Name == "Agent" || ur.Role!.Name == "Admin"))
        .Select(u => new { u.Id, u.DisplayName })
        .ToListAsync(ct);

    if (candidates.Count == 0) return null;

    var loads = await db.Tickets
        .Where(t => t.AssignedToUserId != null && t.Status != "Closed")
        .GroupBy(t => t.AssignedToUserId!.Value)
        .Select(g => new { UserId = g.Key, Count = g.Count() })
        .ToDictionaryAsync(x => x.UserId, x => x.Count, ct);

    var winner = candidates
        .OrderBy(c => loads.TryGetValue(c.Id, out var n) ? n : 0)
        .ThenBy(c => c.Id) // deterministic tiebreak
        .First();

    return await db.Users.FindAsync(new object?[] { winner.Id }, ct);
}
```

- Use the returned user as the assignee (skip `TryResolveAssignee` in this branch). If the pool is empty, leave the ticket unassigned — do **not** return an error.
- After `SaveChangesAsync`, if the ticket ended up with an `AssignedToUserId`, call `CreateAssignedNotificationAsync(ticket, db)`.

### 8 — `PUT /api/tickets/{id}` (Update): resolved-at + reassign notification

**File:** `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/TicketsController.cs`, `Update` handler (~lines 370–415)

- Capture `previousStatus`, `previousAssigneeId` before applying updates.
- After validation, when applying `Status`:
  - If new status is `"Closed"` and previous status was not: `ticket.ResolvedAtUtc = DateTime.UtcNow;`
  - If new status is not `"Closed"` and previous status was `"Closed"`: `ticket.ResolvedAtUtc = null;`
- After `SaveChangesAsync`, if `ticket.AssignedToUserId is not null` and `ticket.AssignedToUserId != previousAssigneeId`, call `CreateAssignedNotificationAsync(ticket, db)` and save. Same call is invoked from Create (§7) and from Story 08's manual assignment path — both converge here.
- Then run the same lazy escalation check as in §5 and call `EnsureEscalationNotificationAsync` if applicable.

### 9 — Notification helpers (private, in `TicketsController.cs`)

```csharp
private static async Task CreateAssignedNotificationAsync(Ticket ticket, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    if (ticket.AssignedToUserId is null) return;

    db.Notifications.Add(new Notification
    {
        UserId = ticket.AssignedToUserId.Value,
        TicketId = ticket.Id,
        Type = "Assigned",
        Message = $"You have been assigned ticket #{ticket.Id}.",
        IsRead = false,
        CreatedAtUtc = DateTime.UtcNow
    });
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
}

private static async Task EnsureEscalationNotificationAsync(Ticket ticket, AppDbContext db, CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    if (ticket.AssignedToUserId is null) return;

    var exists = await db.Notifications.AnyAsync(n =>
        n.TicketId == ticket.Id &&
        n.Type == "Escalated" &&
        !n.IsRead, ct);
    if (exists) return;

    db.Notifications.Add(new Notification
    {
        UserId = ticket.AssignedToUserId.Value,
        TicketId = ticket.Id,
        Type = "Escalated",
        Message = $"Ticket #{ticket.Id} has breached its SLA.",
        IsRead = false,
        CreatedAtUtc = DateTime.UtcNow
    });
    await db.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
}
```

De-dup rule (per Decision 5): unread `Escalated` notification for the same `TicketId` blocks new ones. When the user marks it read, and the ticket is still escalated on next access, a fresh one is allowed.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty Agent/Admin pool on create.** `PickLeastLoadedAssigneeAsync` returns `null` → ticket is created unassigned, no notification, no error. Enforced in `Create` in `TicketsController.cs` (see §7).
- **Explicit `null` in `assignedToUserId` on create.** Treated as "leave unassigned"; auto-assignment does **not** kick in. Distinguish by using an internal flag (e.g. inspect whether the JSON property was present) or by convention: only trigger auto-assignment when the caller sends no property at all. Verify by adding a test that posts `{ "assignedToUserId": null, ... }` and confirms unassigned result. Implemented in `Create`.
- **Priority not in `SlaTargets`.** `ComputeDueDates` falls back to `Normal`. Enforced in the helper (§3). No exception.
- **Ticket already escalated, still escalated, existing unread notification.** `EnsureEscalationNotificationAsync` short-circuits via the `AnyAsync(... !n.IsRead)` check — no duplicate.
- **Ticket reopened (`Closed` → `Open`).** `ResolvedAtUtc` is cleared; if the resolution due date has already passed, `IsEscalated` becomes `true` on the very next read, and a fresh escalation notification is created if none unread exists. Enforced in `Update` (§8).
- **Marking a notification read for a ticket that is still escalated.** The next `List`/`Get` may create a new escalation notification (the previous one is now read, so the de-dup check doesn't block). This is intentional per the intake and per Decision 5.
- **Concurrent list requests both detecting new escalation.** The `AnyAsync` + `Add` pattern is not transactional; a second concurrent request could insert a duplicate. Mitigation for this story: accept the small race (rare; only two identical rows at worst; user can mark both read). Document explicitly; do not introduce locking/serialization infrastructure — out of scope.
- **User whose account has been deleted appears in notifications.** FK cascade on `Notification.UserId` → `Users(Id)` deletes them automatically.
- **Ticket deleted while notifications exist.** FK cascade on `Notification.TicketId` → `Tickets(Id)` deletes them automatically.
- **Notification marked read by wrong user.** `POST /api/notifications/{id}/read` returns `404` when `UserId != callerId` — never `403`, to avoid confirming existence of another user's notification id.
- **Clock skew across servers.** All computations use `DateTime.UtcNow` server-side, matching the rest of the codebase's UTC convention.
- **Interval bell polling with no auth token.** If the JWT has expired, `httpClient` interceptor already redirects to `/login` (Story 03). The bell simply stops updating; no special-case needed.
- **RTL layout of the bell.** Use logical Tailwind classes (`ps-*`, `pe-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`) so the badge and dropdown flip correctly.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Migration name:** `AddSlaAndNotifications`. Adds two nullable columns to `Tickets` and creates the `Notifications` table plus indexes. Purely additive; no data backfill required — new columns start `NULL` on existing rows, which is semantically correct (no first response recorded, not yet resolved).
- **Rollback:** `dotnet ef migrations remove` before applying, or `dotnet ef database update <previous-migration>` after applying. Because the migration is additive, rollback is safe even after data has been written — dropping the `Notifications` table is destructive but the entity does not participate in any pre-existing FK, so no cascade damage.
- **Half-applied state risk:** If the migration is applied but the new code is not yet deployed, existing behavior is unchanged — the extra columns are simply ignored. If the code is deployed but the migration is not, `Create`/`Update`/`List`/`Get` will throw at the first DB read/write. Deploy migration **before** code (standard order for additive migrations here).
